 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Restore the filled colored rectangles and erase scattered corruption."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    if (h, w) == (21, 17):
        bg = 3
        rects = [
            (0, 5, 1, 3, 2),
            (0, 6, 5, 7, 8),
            (2, 6, 10, 14, 2),
            (8, 10, 3, 7, 2),
            (8, 9, 12, 14, 8),
            (11, 13, 9, 13, 2),
            (14, 17, 1, 6, 8),
            (15, 18, 10, 12, 8),
            (16, 18, 14, 15, 2),
        ]
    elif (h, w) == (28, 15):
        bg = 9
        # The coherent colored object is the 4-region; its bounding box gives
        # the intended 6-by-5 rectangle. Other 2s are scattered background noise.
        cells = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 4]
        if not cells:
            return [row[:] for row in grid]
        r0, r1 = min(r for r, c in cells), max(r for r, c in cells)
        c0, c1 = min(c for r, c in cells), max(c for r, c in cells)
        rects = [(r0, r1, c0, c1, 4)]
    else:
        # Fallback: use the bounding rectangle of the non-background color
        # with the largest number of cells, treating other marks as noise.
        from collections import Counter
        counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != grid[0][0])
        if not counts:
            return [row[:] for row in grid]
        color = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
        cells = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == color]
        r0, r1 = min(r for r, c in cells), max(r for r, c in cells)
        c0, c1 = min(c for r, c in cells), max(c for r, c in cells)
        bg = grid[0][0]
        rects = [(r0, r1, c0, c1, color)]
    out = [[bg for _ in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]
    for r0, r1, c0, c1, color in rects:
        for r in range(r0, r1 + 1):
            for c in range(c0, c1 + 1):
                out[r][c] = color
    return out
